questions.question: Why do multi-agent software teams use parallel git worktrees per coder rather than having all coders work on the same branch?
options: Parallel worktrees reduce GitHub API rate limits
Each coder works on an isolated branch without interfering with others; the branches are merged by a coordinator after all subtasks complete
git worktrees are required by the A2A protocol for agent isolation
Parallel branches are cheaper to test in Daytona sandboxes
questions.explanation: Each coder gets a fresh `git worktree add` branch plus a Daytona sandbox. This isolates implementation, prevents mid-work conflicts, and allows all coders to run simultaneously before a merge coordinator integrates the branches.

questions.question: What is 'token amplification' and why is it the key efficiency metric for multi-agent systems?
options: The number of LLM API calls needed to complete a task vs. a single-agent baseline
Total tokens across all roles for a task divided by single-agent tokens; measures the overhead cost of role boundaries and handoff context
The compression ratio achieved by summarizing subtask outputs before passing them to the reviewer
The fraction of tokens in the architect's plan that the coders actually act on
questions.explanation: Token amplification is (coder + reviewer + tester + architect tokens) / single-agent tokens for the same task. Every role boundary adds summary prompts and handoff context; the multi-agent system only wins per dollar if the efficiency gain exceeds this overhead.

questions.question: What constraint prevents the reviewer from approving diffs it authored?
options: The reviewer runs on a different LLM provider than the coders
The task-board schema marks each diff with the authoring agent; the reviewer cannot emit 'approved' on messages it sent
GitHub branch protection prevents the reviewer's GitHub App token from merging its own PRs
The tester role automatically re-runs tests if it detects the reviewer approved its own code
questions.explanation: The design explicitly states the reviewer cannot approve diffs it authored or changes it proposed. The task-board typed messages track authorship, enforcing this conflict-of-interest guard.

questions.question: What is the A2A protocol and how is it used in this capstone?
options: An Anthropic API specification for chaining Claude model calls in a single session
Google's 2025 spec for typed inter-agent messages; used to define structured message types (plan_request, subtask, diff_ready, approved, etc.) across role boundaries
An AWS IAM policy framework for restricting agent service account permissions
An OpenAI streaming protocol that allows partial function-call results
questions.explanation: A2A is Google's 2025 inter-agent messaging protocol used here to define typed task-board messages. Each crossing of a role boundary is a structured A2A message (e.g., subtask, diff_ready, review_feedback), making handoffs explicit and traceable.

questions.question: What does the post-mortem handoff-failure histogram track after a 50-issue SWE-bench run?
options: Per-coder token spending and the number of Daytona sandbox timeouts
The distribution of failed issues by the role-boundary failure type (plan too vague, merge conflict, reviewer false-approve, tester flake)
Per-model API error rates grouped by provider
The number of issues where the merge coordinator introduced a regression
questions.explanation: For each failed issue, the post-mortem identifies the handoff that broke it and bins the issue under a failure type. This histogram tells the team which coordination mechanism needs the most improvement.

questions.question: What model is assigned to each role in the default configuration of this multi-agent team?
options: All roles use Claude Sonnet 4.7 for consistency and comparable cost analysis
Architect uses Opus 4.7, coders use Sonnet 4.7, reviewer uses GPT-5.4, tester uses Gemini 2.5 Pro
Architect uses GPT-5.4, coders use Opus 4.7, reviewer uses Gemini 2.5 Pro, tester uses Sonnet 4.7
All roles use a locally hosted Llama 3.3 70B to minimize API cost
questions.explanation: The capstone assigns the most capable model (Opus 4.7) to the architect for planning, Sonnet 4.7 to the N coders, GPT-5.4 to the reviewer, and Gemini 2.5 Pro to the tester. This leverages model strengths per role.
